notes: PSA 27 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.46. Prostate volume 59 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.87.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment decision following confirmed prostate cancer diagnosis and recent MRI findings.

The patient is a 69-year-old office administrator with a history of prostate cancer diagnosed on biopsy in July 2023. He has been followed up with serial PSA measurements showing a rapid rise from 3.7 ng/mL in July 2022 to 27.0 ng/mL in January 2025. He is married and lives with his partner, who is his primary contact. He is an ex-smoker, having quit in 2005 after a 38 pack-year history. He does not consume alcohol and performs light weight-training twice a week. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 3/35. He is currently under the care of a pain clinic for chronic shoulder pain. He has no active medications and no known allergies.

On DRE, a firm nodule is palpated with suspected extracapsular extension, consistent with clinical stage cT3a. General examination is unremarkable with stable vitals and no signs of metastatic disease.
